title: Urgent warning to Aussies with superannuation: Ditch this fund now
text:
By SARAH BROOKES - SENIOR REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  12:48 AEST, 31 August 2026   |  Updated:  13:10 AEST, 31 August 2026

10

View  comments

More than 66,000 Australian workers will receive letters warning that their super fund has underperformed after a major industry fund managing almost $7.5 billion became the only MySuper product in the country to fail a key regulator test.

Queensland-based construction industry fund BUSSQ failed the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority's annual performance assessment, meaning it must notify affected members that their retirement savings product is underperforming.

APRA released the results of its 2026 annual super performance test on Friday, assessing 547 products covering 61 per cent of member benefits held in APRA-regulated superannuation funds.

BUSSQ's default option was the only one of Australia's 50 MySuper products to fail.

The result also means BUSSQ's MySuper product could be barred from accepting new members if it fails the test again next year.

BUSSQ returned just 5.89 per cent in the year to June 30, well below the 9.5 per cent median return for growth funds, as its high exposure to cash and fixed income weighed on its performance.

Super Consumers Australia chief executive Xavier O'Halloran said it was extremely concerning that BUSSQ had no obligation to issue the same warning to retirees invested in its equivalent retirement product.

'Two people invested in essentially the same product should not get different protections just because one has retired,' he said.

More than 66,000 Australian workers will be warned their super fund has underperformed after Queensland-based BUSSQ became the only MySuper product in the country to fail APRA's annual performance test

'If there is a warning about poor performance, retirees deserve to hear it too.'

BUSSQ chief executive Damian Wills said the fund was taking the result seriously and had already made significant changes to its investment strategy in an effort to improve returns for members.

'We conducted a holistic review of our investment strategy last year and implemented material changes to our investment strategy and portfolio, removing underperforming investment managers and moving to more indexed equity mandates,' he said.

A further 11 trustee-directed products offered through major wealth management platforms also failed the test, including products from Insignia Financial-owned MLC, AMP and the Bendigo Superannuation Plan, owned by Betashares.

Five of those products have now failed APRA's performance assessment for at least two consecutive years.

APRA said six trustees were responsible for the 12 failed products, with poor investment performance, rather than high administration fees, the primary driver of this year's failures.

Meanwhile, the top 10 performing growth super funds have been revealed, with UniSuper Growth leading the pack with a 12.3 per cent return in the year to June 30, 2026.

NGS Super Diversified and CFS FirstChoice Growth were next, both returning 11.5 per cent, followed by Hostplus Balanced at 10.8 per cent and UniSuper Balanced at 10.4 per cent.

Team Super Growth and legalsuper MySuper Balanced both returned 10.2 per cent, while PSSap MySuper Balanced delivered 10 per cent.

Rounding out the top 10 were GESB Super My GESB Super at 9.9 per cent and Vanguard Super SaveSmart Growth at 9.8 per cent.
